rule: A question is here because a decision cannot be made until it is answered. Each row states what is known, what is missing, the measurement that would produce it, and what it blocks.

rows.question: Is the NFL.com injury report a lawful source for a row-level published database?
rows.why_it_blocks: The whole availability layer, and the compliance of the published site. NFL.com's Terms of Use prohibit systematic retrieval to compile a database without written consent.
rows.known: The Terms are published and were read. The repository currently retrieves nfl.com/injuries on a schedule and publishes row-level designations. Flag F51 records the conflict and is marked 'needs review'.
rows.missing: Written consent, or a legal reading that the use is permitted, or a decision to publish aggregates only.
rows.how_to_discover: Read the Terms in full with the owner; request written permission from the NFL; or restructure the site to aggregates plus a link to the official page.
rows.blocks: Every availability claim, the injury-surprise ablation (W09), and the private/public split (SI-11).

rows.question: Which price source is approved, and what is its fetch schedule?
rows.why_it_blocks: Every ROI number. Without an opening and a closing price with a fetch time, a backtest cannot distinguish a real edge from a line that moved after the bet.
rows.known: One closing-price series exists in the third-party extract (nflverse). There is no opening price, no fetch time, and no approval. The readiness register marks the price store BLOCKED.
rows.missing: An approved source, a licence, and a fetch schedule.
rows.how_to_discover: Request documented API access from a data vendor; record the fetch time on every pull; store the raw payload hash.
rows.blocks: The price-snapshot store (PR-01), prospectively scored strategies, and any ROI claim.

rows.question: Are the historical results and closing lines in the third-party extract identical to the official NFL record for every game in the backtest sample?
rows.why_it_blocks: The proper-score intervals (the model side skill is -0.0413, the total -0.0346, the moneyline -0.0714) are computed on the priced games in the extract, almost all of them from the extract and not from an official page. A systematic error there would move every interval.
rows.known: The 2026 schedule and standings in this repository were checked against nfl.com. The historical seasons were not checked game by game.
rows.missing: A game-by-game reconciliation of the extract against official Game Books for 1999-2025.
rows.how_to_discover: Fetch the official Game Book PDF for a random sample of 50 games per season and compare the final score and the closing line.
rows.blocks: Confidence in every historical interval; the results corpus (PR-02, PR-09).

rows.question: What does an official depth chart actually mean when a club publishes more than one player at rank 1?
rows.why_it_blocks: The backup-deficiency feature: 149 club/unit/position slots list more than one rank-1 player, so 'column 1 is the starter' fabricates a starter the club never named.
rows.known: The club charts were read. Shared rank-1 slots and empty slots exist. No club publishes an official snap share in the same document.
rows.missing: An official snap-count source, or Game Book starters, to turn a chart into playing time.
rows.how_to_discover: Publish depth as groups (rank-1 set, rank-2 set) and confirm the starter from Game Books, not from the chart order.
rows.blocks: The deficiency matrix, the injury-surprise ablation, and every '2nd string' claim.

rows.question: What is the correct number of tests to charge for when a rule family shares inputs?
rows.why_it_blocks: The leaderboard's multiplicity adjustment. Twelve rules were tested; several share the same model inputs (S01/S02, S03/S04), so they are not independent and a Bonferroni charge at alpha = 0.00417 is conservative in the wrong direction.
rows.known: The twelve rule p-values and the six market-test p-values are both computed and published.
rows.missing: A pre-registered rule for the effective number of independent tests in each family.
rows.how_to_discover: Estimate the correlation matrix of the rule signals and use the effective-number-of-tests formula; pre-register the choice before applying it.
rows.blocks: Any claim that a rule cleared the multiplicity gate.

rows.question: Does the rating model's side/total/moneyline deficit against the closing line (-0.0413 side, -0.0346 total, -0.0714 moneyline) reflect a model defect or an information disadvantage?
rows.why_it_blocks: Whether to spend effort on features or to accept that the closing line is already the best available forecast, which the evidence currently supports.
rows.known: The paired comparison in the repository's own research run shows the market's absolute error on the closing spread is smaller than the model's. The two-estimator test shows the ratings do not beat a season-mean baseline on the holdout (difference -0.0136, interval -0.2288 to +0.2188).
rows.missing: A model with information the closing line does not already contain (availability surprise, weather, referee).
rows.how_to_discover: Add one feature at a time and require the incremental-information weight to be positive with |t| > 2 before keeping it.

rows.question: Which of the brief's own numbered references (VR-xx, VQ-xx) can be traced to a dated source?
rows.why_it_blocks: Reproducing the brief's findings. Several rows quote VR/VQ numbers that no artifact in the repository contains.
rows.known: The references appear in the brief and in earlier sessions' notes; the underlying captures are not all present.
rows.missing: The dated captures those references point at.
rows.how_to_discover: Re-capture each cited page and record the fetch time and hash; where the capture no longer exists, mark the reference untraceable.
rows.blocks: Only the traceability of the brief's claims; nothing on the leaderboard depends on them.

rows.question: How should a parlay be validated when the legs are dependent?
rows.why_it_blocks: Ranking any parlay or same-game parlay. The product of marginal probabilities is invalid under dependence.
rows.known: The repository prices every two-leg parlay from the observed legs and publishes the correlation ratio, but it does not validate a joint distribution. The proper-score page leaves the parlay and same-game-parlay markets blank for this reason.
rows.missing: A directly validated joint probability, plus the operator's void and push rules.
rows.how_to_discover: Model the joint distribution of the two legs (bivariate normal for spread+total in one game) and validate it out of sample before ranking anything.
rows.blocks: The parlay and prop-combo divisions of the leaderboard.

rows.question: What is the minimum live sample before a strategy can be called live rather than paper?
rows.why_it_blocks: Promotion. The demotion gate is armed but nothing can be promoted, because nothing is live.
rows.known: A promotion threshold is not pre-registered. The demotion thresholds (50, 100 and 12 bets) are pre-registered in 31 registration records.
rows.missing: A pre-registered promotion rule that mirrors the demotion rule.
rows.how_to_discover: Write the promotion rule now, before the first live bet, and commit it with the demotion rule text.
rows.blocks: Any live status, and therefore any reward.

rows.question: Are player-prop prices obtainable at all, and if not, should the prop division exist?
rows.why_it_blocks: The prop, prop-combo and same-game-parlay divisions have no price and therefore no score.
rows.known: No official or book-level prop price exists in this repository. Projections and correlations are published; no prop bet is scored.
rows.how_to_discover: Same route as Q02. Until then the divisions stay published as empty with the reason.
rows.blocks: Three of the six leaderboard divisions.

rows.question: Should the site publish row-level official data at all, or only derived aggregates plus links?
rows.why_it_blocks: The public/private split (readiness SI-11) and Q01.
rows.known: Roughly 2,071 table rows with official source links are published today, many of them row-level injury and depth entries.
rows.how_to_discover: Take the legal reading first, then decide which rows move behind an access control.

rows.question: Does the injury designation level predict playing time at all?
rows.why_it_blocks: Using any designation as a feature. The brief rejects a level outright and asks for an empirical calibration of 'Questionable'.
rows.known: The designation counts are captured weekly; no play-rate-per-designation study has been run against official inactive lists.
rows.missing: Official inactive lists joined to participation for several seasons.
rows.how_to_discover: Join the weekly designations to the official inactive list and the snap share, then compute the play rate per designation with a binomial interval.
